h: Tips for a Big Day Out in the Weald
p: Knockhatch sits on the edge of Hailsham, handy for the A22, so it's easy to reach from Eastbourne, Lewes and the villages across the Weald. Because it combines animals and adventure play, the best approach is usually to alternate between the two. Watch a display or visit a few animals, then let the kids loose for a run around, then head back to the animals once they've burned off the excess energy. Everyone stays happier that way, including the grown-ups.

If you're visiting with a mix of ages, it's worth agreeing a meeting point in case groups split up, as older children often want to head off and tackle the bigger play areas while toddlers stick to the gentler bits. Sun cream and a hat in summer, waterproofs at other times. It's a good-value way to fill a whole day, so pack enough snacks to keep everyone going between meals.

The surrounding countryside is full of history. Michelham Priory, near Upper Dicker, is ringed by a medieval water-filled moat and has gardens, a watermill and old buildings to explore. Herstmonceux Castle, a striking fifteenth-century brick castle, has beautiful grounds and is a short drive east of Hailsham. Pevensey Castle, where William the Conqueror is said to have landed in 1066, sits closer to the coast with Roman walls still standing around it. Add an evening on Eastbourne seafront, with its grand Victorian pier and the bandstand, and you've got a weekend packed with variety. Fancy one more view? Beachy Head's towering white cliffs are just beyond Eastbourne for a breezy clifftop walk.
